changes: An agent no longer freezes during heavy web research: it can hold many more connections, and it recovers by itself if it gets stuck.

Meetings: the agent can listen the whole time without a wake word, set reminders when asked, join from calendar invites, join signed in to its Google account, and act on a meeting afterwards by your instructions.
Your firewall's pages (Logs, Doctor, Website logins) have the ControlClaw look, and the page an agent sends you to add a login works well on a phone.
Screenshots of a browser tab that is not in front no longer time out, and unused search providers are switched off.
Wake chimes in meetings are louder and play at a steady level.
Wake chimes in meetings are now heard: the agent's microphone no longer turns them down.
Doctor offers a list of current models, starting on GPT-6.1 Sol, and opens with the agent you came from.
Each agent's pages have a Doctor link, and the firewall's Logs page links to Doctor.
Website logins work with short passwords and PINs, HTTP sign-in prompts and XML forms.
The login alarm no longer blocks pages by mistake, and a password a site shows back is hidden from the agent.
Website logins: save logins on the firewall, and your agents sign in to sites without ever seeing the password.
Your agent can ask you for a login with a secure link instead of in chat, and handles two-step codes.
Firewall Doctor repairs the firewall itself, even when its pages are down.
Doctor works when an agent's management service is down, and can be started from the firewall.
The firewall no longer fills its log with thousands of disk-key checks.
Changing or removing a fallback model works, and a change the agent refuses now says so.
The health check no longer fails on slow ChatGPT models, and shows OpenClaw status unknown instead of stopped.
Firewall Logs loads on older firewalls, and says when the firewall needs an update.
Your firewall has a Logs page that shows each of its services and the last update.
Download workspace saves a readable copy of your agent: its files, memory, conversations, meetings and calls.
Meetings join again after the latest OpenClaw update, and a failed join now says why.
The Doctor tab shows a quick health status and a Check that finds problems and suggests fixes.
Agent pages share one look with a Back to console button, and Meetings has a new list and a page for each meeting.
Agents and firewalls show a version number and what changed in each update.
First numbered release: agents and firewalls now show a version instead of a build code.
